title: Signatures of inter-sideband coherence in the resonance fluorescence spectrum of an acoustically-modulated quantum dot
authors: Rafał A. Bogaczewicz, Hubert J. Krenner, Paweł Machnikowski
abstract: We theoretically investigate the inter-sideband phase coherence within the resonance fluorescence spectrum of an acoustically modulated quantum dot using a filtered-field formalism for a Mach-Zehnder configuration. We demonstrate that geometric slant of the interferograms provides an indicator of phase coherence that is resilient to environmental white noise. Specifically, noise-induced spectral diffusion reduces the global fringe intensity, while leaving the characteristic inclination strictly invariant. Our findings establish a framework for verifying single-photon coherence between spectral sidebands, essential for frequency-bin encoding and scalable quantum networking in realistic, noisy solid-state architectures.
summary: The authors developed a theoretical framework to measure inter-sideband phase coherence in an acoustically-modulated quantum dot using resonance fluorescence. They show that the geometric slant of the resulting 2D interferogram is a robust diagnostic tool that remains visible even when subjected to environmental white noise. This technique offers a practical method to verify quantum coherence in solid-state quantum emitters.
main_problem: The paper theoretically investigates the inter-sideband phase coherence within the resonance fluorescence spectrum of an acoustically-modulated quantum dot.
main_result: The geometric slant of the two-dimensional interferogram serves as a robust, noise-resilient indicator of phase coherence between spectral sidebands, essential for quantum networking.
method: The analysis employs a filtered-field formalism applied to a Mach-Zehnder interferometer setup, analyzing time-dependent correlation functions.
model_or_system: The system is a quantum dot (modeled as a two-level system) coupled to an optical field and modulated by Surface Acoustic Waves (SAWs). The fluorescence spectrum contains a central line and sidebands.

important_parameters: Acoustic modulation frequency ($\omega_A$), environmental white noise diffusion coefficient ($D$), and the detuning ($\delta\omega$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system reaches a stationary state and that the acoustic modulation provides sufficient phase stability to protect the coherence signature.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between coherent (slanted) and incoherent (vertical) interference patterns in the 2D interferograms, demonstrating the characteristic slant under different sideband selections and noise levels.
paper_structure: The paper builds from deriving the intensity components using autocorrelation functions, establishing the diagnostic tool (the fringe slant) via the phase-matching condition, and finally demonstrating its robustness against environmental noise.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, measurable spectroscopic signature (the fringe slant) to diagnose fundamental quantum coherence in solid-state emitters, which is crucial for developing scalable quantum information platforms.

figures.caption: Fig. 1. Schematic representation of the theoretical setup. Left: A QD with a time-modulated transition frequency (indicated by the shaded area). Center: Two Lorentzian filters with band- width Γ are tuned to selected sidebands in the output signal. Right: The selected beams enter a Mach-Zehnder interferome- ter. One arm incorporates an external frequency shift δω and a time delay τd.

Fig. 2. Incoherent (a, c) and coherent (b, d) superpositions of the light beams from the ZPL (k1 = 0) and the first PSB (k2 = 1). Panels (a, b) show the noise-free case (D = 0), while (c, d) incorporate white noise (D = 0.05ωA). Here ωL = ω0 and δω = 0. Black and white dashed lines in (b, d) represent the analytical trajectories for maximal and minimal intensities, respectively.

Fig. 3. Coherent interference intensities without noise (D = 0) and under resonant (ωL = ω0) driving. (a) Superposition of the ZPL and the first right PSB, (k1, k2) = (0, 1), under the resonance shift condition δω = ωA. (b) Superposition of the left and right first-order PSBs, (k1, k2) = (−1, 1), without an external shift (δω = 0). Black and white dashed lines represent the analytical trajectories for maximal and minimal intensities, respectively.

Fig. 4. Coherent interference intensities for ωL = ω0 + ωA/3 under the (k1, k2) = (0, 1) configuration. Panels (a, c) show δω = 0, while (b, d) show δω = ωA/3. Results for the noise- free case (a, b) and D = 0.05ωA (c, d). Black and white dashed lines denote the analytical trajectories for maximal and mini- mal intensities, respectively.
